targets.title: Corrective feedback and learner uptake: Negotiation of form in communicative classrooms
targets.evidence_quote:
Working in groups, the graduate students (students
in an MA-TESL program, and doctoral students in a related program; a combination of practicing

targets.outcome_quote:
First, participants expressed surprise both at the results of all groups in the class – that is,
that recasts were the most frequent type of feedback given, and the least successful in
eliciting student uptake – and at the similarity with the findings of the Lyster and Ranta
study they were replicating.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Authors explicitly compare the classroom replications with the original and describe similar findings on recast frequency and uptake. One group having another dominant feedback type is not framed as an overall contrast with the original; authors describe the findings across groups as remarkably similar.

reasoning: Full article identity and authors match. The primary pedagogical case study also reports new classroom data from partial replications and explicitly compares their findings to Lyster and Ranta. One original paper, not four classroom groups. Other teacher-cognition and feedback references are background.
